blocks.prompt: 8. A sum of Rs. 5000 is invested [printed as 'inverted'] at 8% simple interest per year. Calculate the interest at the end of each year. Do these interests form an A.P.? If so find the interest at the end of 20 years making use of this fact.
blocks.explanation:
Simple interest is always worked out on the original Rs. 5000, so the same amount is earned every year.
The total interest at the end of each year then grows by a fixed amount: an A.P.
Plan: interest for one year; list the totals; check the differences; use \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) with \(n = 20\).
steps:
Given: \(P = 5000\), simple interest 8% per year.
To find: the interest at the end of each year, whether it is an A.P., and the interest after 20 years.
Method: \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) once we know the list is an A.P.

Interest for one year
\[\dfrac{8}{100} \times 5000 = 400\]
Why: 8% of 5000.

Interest at the end of each year
\[400,\ 800,\ 1200,\ 1600,\ \ldots\]
Why: Each year the same Rs. 400 is added to the total interest.

Check whether it is an A.P.
\[800 - 400 = 400\]
\[1200 - 800 = 400\]
\[a_1 = 400,\ d = 400\]
Why: Consecutive differences are equal, so yes, it is an A.P.

Interest after 20 years
\[a_{20} = 400 + (20 - 1)(400)\]
\[= 400 + 7600 = 8000\]
Why: The interest at the end of 20 years is the 20th term.
blocks.final_answer: Interests 400, 800, 1200, ... form an A.P.; interest after 20 years = Rs. 8000

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints "is inverted at 8% simple interest"; it should read "is invested". The mathematics is not affected.
